title: Modeling LLM Reasoning Dynamics with Structural Representations
abstract: arXiv:2611.23749v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Language-model reasoning alternates between sustained activities and local operations. We study how this temporal structure predicts continuation and the computation needed to analyze it. T/E/S combines text, local events, and spans of activity. Across reasoning and information-seeking tasks, events and spans improve next-outcome prediction in 70 of 76 evaluation groups for a Transformer and 74 of 76 for Qwen with LoRA. Span duration and preceding events are associated with transitions, and retaining event history across span boundaries improves prediction. We formulate budget-allocation counting and action-conditional continuation queries, prove counting hardness under explicit encodings, and derive conditions for affordable decision certification. In finite-process experiments, bounds that cancel shared continuation mass recover the same optimal actions as full dynamic programming while reducing mean inference CPU time by 77.7%. On 71

translated_title: 基于结构化表示的大语言模型推理动态建模
translated_abstract: 语言模型的推理在持续性活动与局部操作之间交替进行。我们研究这种时间结构如何预测后续走向，以及分析它所需的计算。T/E/S 方法将文本、局部事件和活动跨度结合起来。在推理与信息检索任务上，事件和跨度特征在76个评估组中的70个提升了一个 Transformer 的下一步结果预测，在76个中的74个提升了使用 LoRA 的 Qwen 的预测。跨度持续时间与前置事件和状态转换相关，并且在跨度边界之间保留事件历史能够改善预测。我们形式化了预算分配计数问题和动作条件延续查询，证明了在显式编码下计数问题的计算难度，并推导出低成本决策认证的可行条件。在有限过程实验中，通过抵消共享延续质量的边界方法能够获得与完整动态规划相同的最优动作，同时将平均推理 CPU 时间降低77.7%。在71…
tldr: 该论文提出 T/E/S 结构化表示（文本、局部事件、活动跨度）来建模大语言模型推理的时间动态，显著提升下一步结果预测，并证明相关计数问题为计算困难，同时给出可将推理CPU时间降低77.7%且保持最优决策的高效认证方法。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes T/E/S structural representations (text, local events, and activity spans) to model the temporal dynamics of LLM reasoning, improving next-outcome prediction, proving counting hardness for related queries, and deriving efficient bounds that reduce inference CPU time by 77.7% while preserving optimal decisions.
